From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: OTLP interop & commercial integration — tech scope and MAP

Hi Sarah & Emma,

Thanks again for taking time last week. Following our product/alliance sync I promised a short note to pull together the technical scope and a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align engineering and GTM timelines.

High-level asks:
- Confirm Datadog/Grafana endpoints you’d like us to validate (OTLP/HTTP, OTLP/gRPC, Datadog agent compatibility).
- Decide whether we certify a managed collector (Redwood-hosted OTLP relay) or provide a reference config for customer-managed OTel stacks.
- Agree on an initial co-sell bundle and a small pilot cohort (3 customers) for Q3.

I attached a short integration spec and a draft MAP (redwood-datadog-grafana-map.xlsx) with proposed owners and dates. Suggested next steps: quick technical breakout with Marcus, then a follow-up commercial sync to lock customer targets and marketing assets.

Are you available for a 45-min tech deep-dive on Tuesday 6/1 or Wednesday 6/2? Marcus will cover collector compatibility and our prefix/KV caching considerations for telemetry throughput.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0186

Laura — great framing, thanks.

Quick answers:
- Datadog prefers OTLP/gRPC for high-throughput telemetry; we also support OTLP/HTTP for constrained environments. We can validate both.
- For certification, Datadog is open to a hybrid approach: list a Redwood-hosted OTLP relay as the recommended pattern for fast onboarding, plus a reference config for customer-managed collectors.
- Pilot: we can commit two logos from our side (one finserv and one SaaS mid-market). EMMA: are you able to bring a Grafana customer for the third?

Tech deep-dive: Tue 6/1 10:30–11:15 PT works for the Datadog engineering pair. Please send calendar invite and a short agenda.

Adding a couple tech notes ahead of the call:
- Relay options: 1) stateless OTLP relay (simple forwarder) 2) stateful relay with short-term KV cache to dedupe and reduce backend load. We recommend starting with stateless to reduce complexity for pilot.
- Sampling: if customer-side sampling is aggressive, we will need to surface guidance for preserving parent-child relationships.
- Perf: our internal tests show OTLP/gRPC throughput of ~120k spans/min per relay instance on an A10-class VM; will share slides with per-instance numbers on the call.
- Security: relay will support mTLS and API-key header fallback for older agents.

See you on the call — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
